liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **China Cat Sunflower** (1 review): Garcia sings the second verse of the song twice [12]
- **I Know You Rider** (1 review): The three-part harmony in the song is described as glorious [12]
- **Two Souls In Communion** (1 review): Listener calls this one of the best versions of the song [7]
- **Dark Star** (1 review): Listener describes the playing as some of the hottest ever [8]

## The recordings

- **gd1972-03-23.sbd.miller.100000.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 27 songs; 216 min; rated 4.45/5 by 31 [1]. Said about its sound: The soundboard recording is described as sounding fantastic [10]
- **gd1972-03-23.136683.sbd.sirmick.flac1648**: soundboard; 26 songs; 201 min; rated 5/5 by 2 [2]. Said about its sound: Recording is very clean with only a few pops and clicks removed [2]
- **gd1972-03-23.157068.aud.lamarre.vernon.sirmick.flac24**: audience recording; 20 songs; 129 min [3]
- **gd1972-03-23.sbd.miller.bertha.100298.dvda**: soundboard; 0 songs; 0 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [6]

## Around the show

- Venue was the Academy of Music, formerly the Paramount Theater in the 1940s [7]
- Pigpen and Bob screamed at the end of the song [8]
- Bobby plays the Weather Report Suite intro after the shuffle [1]
- Betty’s 10-inch master reel ends with four minutes of cheering [3]
- Ron McKernan played Hammond B3 and harmonica during the performance [3]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1972-03-23.sbd.miller.100000.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Apogee AD500 -> Dat (48k) [1]. Also: Charlie Miller transferred the recording, which the listener calls his magic; Transfer assigned shnid 100000 to honor Charlie Miller's community contributions; Rob Eaton lent his DATs for the transfer process [1][9][10]
- **gd1972-03-23.136683.sbd.sirmick.flac1648**: taped by Anonomous; transferred by SIRMick; source: Source: sbd > master reel > dat (48k) [2]
- **gd1972-03-23.157068.aud.lamarre.vernon.sirmick.flac24**: taped by Unknown; transferred by Sirmick and Matt Vernon; source: Unknown audience cassette - from the collection of Doug Lamarre [3]. Also: Harvey Lubar’s soundboard has an extra analog generation from cassette transfer [3]
- **gd1972-03-23.sbd.miller.bertha.100298.dvda**: transferred by Charlie Miller and Jay Ashley; source: SBD>>MR>>DAT>>FLAC [6]. Also: Recording was digitally remastered using the Bertha Digital Audio Workstation [6]
